findings.description: The spec requirement mandates that the isolation vocabulary be defined in exactly one location and referenced by both producer and consumer. The dispatch consumer lives in skills/ (e.g. skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py). However, skills/validate-feature/scripts/tests/test_linters.py enforces check_dependency_direction, which forbids any skill from importing 'from src.' or 'import agent_coordinator'. If isolation_contract is placed in agent-coordinator/src/, consumer dispatch in skills/ cannot import it without failing architectural linters and deployment boundaries.
findings.existing_code:
def test_from_src_dot_import_in_skill_fails(self, tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        """'from src.' import inside a skills/ file should be flagged."""
findings.resolution: Place isolation_contract in a shared monorepo package under packages/ (e.g. packages/isolation-contract or an existing shared package like packages/system-one-decisions) where both agent-coordinator/pyproject.toml and skills/pyproject.toml can import it via tool.uv.sources.

findings.description: Having isolation_contract define the precedence resolver by importing get_agent_isolation from src.agents_config while agents_config imports VALID_ISOLATION_MODES from isolation_contract creates a module-level circular import cycle, causing ImportError on partially initialized module.
findings.resolution: Decouple isolation_contract from agents_config: have resolve_isolation accept an optional pre-resolved config isolation value or a config_resolver callable, or lazily import get_agent_isolation inside the function body.

findings.description: The plan assumes dg-04 code exists in the worktree, but on main, model_routing/routing_policy.py and model_routing/api.py do not exist. They reside on the unmerged branch remotes/origin/openspec/implement-the-task-router-vendor-x-location-x-model (PR #605). Implementing dg-05 against main will fail because the routing policy and API prerequisites are missing.

findings.description: The proposed plan states 'reject unrecognized router/config values; use fallback config then none when router unavailable/silent.' In the precedence resolver, an unrecognized non-None router value must NOT fall back to agents.yaml or none; doing so violates the spec scenario 'An unrecognized isolation value is rejected' by proceeding under a silently substituted posture. An invalid value must fail loudly immediately.
findings.existing_code:
#### Scenario: An unrecognized isolation value is rejected

WHEN a value outside the defined vocabulary reaches the dispatch layer
THEN resolution SHALL fail with an explicit error naming the offending value
AND dispatch SHALL NOT proceed under a silently substituted posture.
findings.resolution: Validate any non-None router isolation value before evaluating fallback; raise an explicit error immediately if unrecognized. Fallback to agents.yaml and none applies only when the router is legitimately unreachable or silent (None).

findings.description: AGENTS_SCHEMA defines cli.dispatch_modes with additionalProperties: False. Adding an isolation override to a dispatch mode in agents.yaml will cause load_agents_config() to fail jsonschema validation unless AGENTS_SCHEMA is updated to permit isolation.
findings.resolution: Update AGENTS_SCHEMA under dispatch_modes.additionalProperties.properties to include 'isolation': {'type': 'string', 'enum': sorted(VALID_ISOLATION_MODES)}.

findings.description: Multiple agent entries in agents.yaml share the same agent_type (e.g. claude-local vs claude-remote; codex-local vs codex-remote) with different isolation modes. get_agent_isolation matches only on the first entry with agent.type == agent_type, making remote agent isolation and dispatch mode overrides unresolvable when called with agent_type.
findings.resolution: Allow get_agent_isolation to accept an agent identifier matching either agent.name == identifier or agent.type == identifier, enabling callers targeting specific agent profiles to resolve their configured isolation.

findings.description: The spec requires that the resolved decision record which rung of the ladder produced it (router, agents_config, or none). The plan omits specifying test cases covering rung attribution, router silent fallback, coordinator unreachable fallback, unrecognized router value rejection, and per-mode override precedence.
